new_statements.quote: The syllabic structure is (C1)(C2)V, where C1 can be any consonant phoneme in Table 1, C2 can only be /j/, V is a vowel nucleus, and brackets indicate optional constituents. Duoxu has four contrastive tones on monosyllabic words. In the five-scale pitch system developed by Chao (1930), these tones may be annotated as 53, 44, 34, and 32. Examples include /wu⁵³/ 'wine, beer (155)', /wu⁴⁴/ 'water (21)', /we³⁴/ 'to wear (282)', /wu³²/ 'to be narrow (39)'; /la⁵³ba³²/ 'radish, turnip', /la⁴⁴ma⁴⁴/ 'lama (66)', /la³⁴/ 'god (171)', /la³²/ 'lightning (7); tiger (206)'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Duoxu is described as a tone language with four contrastive lexical tones on monosyllabic words (53, 44, 34, 32 in Chao numerals). The paper has no stress, accent or prominence section for Duoxu and makes no statement about word stress; the only 'prominence' vocabulary (EP/LP/RP patterns) concerns Lizu, not Duoxu.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the paper notes that the 'convergence group' of speakers has a phonemic inventory already identical to Southwest Mandarin, while the tone statement is given for the conservative group
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Duoxu of Mianning county, Sichuan (the only variety; the language is moribund). Chirkova 2014 distinguishes a 'conservative' speaker group, whose phonology (including the four tones) is described, from a 'convergence' group whose phonemic inventory has merged with Southwest Mandarin. The tone-plus-accent ('hybrid') statements in the HDR concern the sister languages Lizu and Ersu, not Duoxu.

new_statements.quote: le lizu et le ersu (dont le système prosodique est du même type que le lizu, voir Chirkova et al. 2015) présentent un contraste marquant avec le duoxu, qui possède un système du type « omnisyllabique », avec un ton pour chaque syllabe. L'organisation prosodique du duoxu est la suivante. Le duoxu a quatre tons lexicaux contrastifs sur les mots monosyllabiques, trois schémas tonals sur les mots disyllabiques avec la racine /ə˞/ en position de deuxième syllabe [...], 15 combinaisons de tons sur des domaines disyllabiques réguliers (mots et expressions), y compris des combinaisons comprenant un ton neutre. [p. 129] — le ersu, le lizu et le duoxu, lesquelles combinent systèmes hybrides de ton et d'accent (le lizu, le ersu) et système omnisyllabique (le duoxu) [p. 122]
new_statements.translation: Lizu and Ersu (whose prosodic system is of the same type as Lizu, see Chirkova et al. 2015) present a marked contrast with Duoxu, which has a system of the 'omnisyllabic' type, with a tone on every syllable. The prosodic organisation of Duoxu is as follows. Duoxu has four contrastive lexical tones on monosyllabic words, three tonal patterns on disyllabic words with the root /ə˞/ in second-syllable position [...], 15 tone combinations on regular disyllabic domains (words and phrases), including combinations containing a neutral tone. [p. 129] — Ersu, Lizu and Duoxu, which combine hybrid systems of tone and accent (Lizu, Ersu) and an omnisyllabic system (Duoxu) [p. 122]

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record is empty. The HDR gives a fuller description than the 2014 paper: Duoxu is an omnisyllabic lexical-tone language (tone on every syllable), explicitly set apart from its sisters Lizu and Ersu, which have hybrid tone-plus-accent (stress) systems. This is the strongest statement available that Duoxu has no word-stress/accent system of the kind its sister languages have, though it is a classification by contrast rather than a sentence 'Duoxu has no stress'. Tone values differ from the 2014 paper (53/31/33/22 vs 53/44/34/32), reflecting a revised instrumental analysis (167 words, Praat) rather than a contradiction of type.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Duoxu has an 'omnisyllabic' tone system with a tone on every syllable: four contrastive lexical tones on monosyllables (53, 31, 33, 22 in this later analysis), three tonal patterns on disyllables with the root /-ə˞/, and 15 tone combinations on regular disyllabic domains including combinations with a neutral tone; disyllabic patterns are juxtapositions of lexical tones, tone sandhi (the mid-falling 31 is realised as low-level 22 in word-initial position, neutralising 31 vs 22 there), and tone + neutral-tone syllables. The HDR explicitly contrasts Duoxu (omnisyllabic tone) with Lizu and Ersu, which 'combine hybrid systems of tone and accent'; no word stress or accent is posited for Duoxu.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none mentioned; no stress of any kind is posited for Duoxu
new_statements.exceptions: neutral-tone syllables (e.g. the classifier /-pu/ in /ɡe³¹-pu/ 'pot'); tone sandhi neutralising 31 vs 22 word-initially; the 25 rising pattern on /-ə˞/ words analysed as a tone combination (22-53 and/or 31-53)
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Duoxu of Mianning county, Sichuan (the only variety; the language is moribund). The tone-plus-accent ('hybrid') statements in the HDR concern the sister languages Lizu and Ersu, not Duoxu.

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Chirkova 2015 phonological sketch at the stated sections/pages. The source is a dedicated phonology paper with acoustic measurements by the language's principal documenter; the classification 'tonal' (four lexical tones, neutral tone = 'weak stress' as a morphologically defined toneless class, no independent word-stress rule) is exactly what it says. Two further open Chirkova works downloaded now (LTBA 2014; HDR 2020) restate the four-tone analysis, and the 2020 HDR explicitly types Duoxu as an omnisyllabic tone system in contrast to the tone-plus-accent systems of Lizu/Ersu, so nothing suggests the classification would change. The only superior description is the 2020 Commercial Press grammar co-authored by Chirkova (print only, Chinese); worth holding for completeness and for the >2-syllable domain, but not expected to alter the record. sources.note: Or-record: Nishida (1973: 115-116) reconstructs the Tosu sound system from the Chinese and Tibetan transcriptions INCLUDING a four-way tonal notation - '—' high even tone, '´' rising tone, '_' low even tone, '`' high falling tone - written on every reconstructed Tosu form (also used in Nishida 1976). A philological reconstruction for the XFYY variety, not an instrumental description; how the categories are derived from the transcribing characters' Mandarin tones is in the phonology chapter (pp. ~115 ff.).
